The Figure, Torah Teaching and Public Work of Rabbi Avraham Mordechai Yitzchaki, the Rav of Porat
The text surveys the work and thought of Rabbi Avraham Mordechai Yitzchaki, known as "the Rav of Porat", and sketches his figure as a spiritual leader who combines a deep kabbalistic tradition with innovative use of technology for spreading Torah. The source describes the unique communal structure of Moshav Porat, in which the rabbi holds exclusive religious authority alongside a secular civil administration, and at its centre the establishment of the "David HaMelech" (King David) beit midrash as a regional focus for the study of the Zohar and the esoteric teaching. The essence of his teaching centres on making Kabbalah accessible as a practical tool for the repair of the soul, with decisive emphasis on the practice of hitbodedut (secluded personal prayer) as the central path of redemption in our generation. Finally, the article highlights the process of digitisation that made the rabbi a figure of worldwide influence, and the efforts to preserve his legacy by training a generation of continuity of young rabbis from his family.
The Figure, Torah Teaching and Public Work of Rabbi Avraham Mordechai Yitzchaki, the Rav of Porat
The Dual-Centred Structure of Moshav Porat and Rabbi Yitzchaki's Leadership
The spiritual leadership of Rabbi Avraham Mordechai Yitzchaki (known by his epithet "the Rav of Porat") in Moshav Porat, which lies within the Lev HaSharon Regional Council, presents a fascinating model of dual authority in a traditional agricultural community in Israel.[1, 2, 3] Whereas the administrative, municipal and economic management of the moshav is entrusted to a local committee and secular and traditional members of the general assembly, the formal and informal spiritual, educational and halakhic authority rests exclusively in the hands of Rabbi Yitzchaki.[1, 2, 3] This division allows the moshav to preserve its modern communal character on the one hand, while deeply anchoring religious and traditional life around fixed institutions on the other.
The core of this activity is concentrated in the "David HaMelech" beit midrash in Moshav Porat, which serves not only as a place of prayer but as the central axis around which the spiritual life of the residents revolves.[1, 2, 4] Under Rabbi Yitzchaki's leadership, the beit midrash has become a regional Torah centre that draws Torah enthusiasts, kabbalists and residents from all over the Sharon region, and thereby makes the residents of the geographical periphery independent of the large urban Torah centres.[1, 4, 5]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Timeline of the Leadership and the Development of the Educational Institutions
An examination of Rabbi Yitzchaki's work over the years shows a long-term and continuous leadership extending over decades.[2, 5] The documentation of his public lessons begins at least in the year 5770 (2010) and continues consistently through the years 5783 (2023), 5784 (2024) and up to the present period in the year 5786 (2026).[1, 2, 5] This historical continuity attests to spiritual-governing stability and to a deep and lasting trust on the part of the local and regional community.
A further significant trend emerging in recent years is the development of a young leadership stratum and of additional rabbis active alongside Rabbi Yitzchaki, such as Rabbi Uriah and Rabbi Akiva Yitzchaki.[5] The involvement of these figures in giving the lessons on the holy Zohar and in leading the beit midrash points to a structured process of generational continuity.[5] The transformation of the beit midrash in Porat from a centre operating on the basis of a single leader's charisma into a communal institution with many lecturers and leaders ensures the survival of the rabbi's Torah teaching for future generations as well, and in effect creates an independent theological school in the heart of the Sharon.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Rabbi's Kabbalistic Teaching and the Connection to the School of HaChalban
Rabbi Yitzchaki's Torah teaching is characterised by a distinct inclination towards the world of the esoteric and Kabbalah, and he is consistently described by his students and listeners as "the kabbalist rabbi".[1, 2, 4] His regular lessons are based on the reading, decoding and practical interpretation of the holy Zohar.[4, 5] At the same time, the rabbi does not leave Kabbalah as an abstract theoretical field intended for a select few alone; he strives to make the most complex kabbalistic concepts accessible and to translate them into practical guidance in the refinement of character traits, in the repair of the soul and in the understanding of the processes of history and redemption.[4, 6]
An integral part of his teaching concerns the supreme importance of the practice of hitbodedut.[6] Rabbi Yitzchaki sees a person's personal and private conversation with his Maker as the most powerful spiritual tool in our generation, and even defines hitbodedut as the central and sole factor that will bring about the salvation and redemption of the people of Israel.[6] This approach creates a close conceptual affinity between him and the teaching of Breslov Hasidism, but it also finds concrete expression in institutional and conceptual ties with the circle of kabbalists associated with Rabbi Chaim Cohen of blessed memory (known as "HaChalban", "the Milkman").
The fact that Rabbi Yitzchaki's lessons on hitbodedut and redemption are uploaded to the official channel of "HaChalban" attests to mutual recognition, theological cooperation and mutual influence between these kabbalistic schools.[6] Both schools share the conception that national redemption will grow out of the inner, personal and simple work of the masses of the House of Israel, and not necessarily out of elitist seclusion in closed courts.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Digitisation of Torah and the Widening of the Bounds of Influence
One of Rabbi Yitzchaki's most prominent achievements in his public work is breaking through the geographical bounds of Moshav Porat by means of a judicious and advanced use of digital media.[1, 4, 5] The rabbi's official YouTube channel (@HaravMiporat) is in practice a global virtual beit midrash.[1, 4, 5] Through regular live broadcasts of lessons on the Zohar, festival sermons and special tikkunim (rectification prayers), the rabbi manages to reach hundreds and thousands of viewers who join the lesson in real time or consume the content in the digital archive.[4, 5]
This process leads to a de-localisation of Torah authority: the rabbi is not only the rabbi of the local settlement who rules on the everyday questions of Porat's residents, but a Torah figure with national and worldwide resonance, who influences diverse audiences that do not belong to the classic religious-Orthodox sector.[1, 4, 5] Making the lessons on the Zohar, the talks of encouragement on hitbodedut and the stories of tzaddikim (such as the miracles of the Baba Elazar Abuhatzeira of blessed memory) accessible in the digital space creates a direct connection with a young audience searching for a path, which finds in the rabbi's teaching a stable spiritual anchor in the modern era.[1, 5, 6]

Summary and Conclusions on the Deeper Trends in the Rabbi's Activity
The work and Torah teaching of Rabbi Avraham Mordechai Yitzchaki reflect the most significant social and religious trends that traditional and religious society in Israel has undergone in recent decades. His unique path outlines several conclusions and deeper insights regarding the character of modern spiritual leadership:
Creating an Alternative Spiritual Centre in the Geographical Periphery
Rabbi Yitzchaki has proved that a central urban location is not needed in order to establish an empire of the study of Kabbalah and the Zohar.[1, 4] Moving the study of the esoteric teaching into the rural space in the heart of the Sharon offers a refreshing alternative for seekers of spirituality who look for quiet, simplicity and a direct connection to nature and the land, which fit well with the foundations of Hasidic and kabbalistic hitbodedut.[6]
A Harmonious Combination of Traditional Authority and New Media
The success of the rabbi's YouTube channel and his online influence show that a leadership that is rooted and conservative in character need not fear technological progress; on the contrary, technology can serve as the most effective tool for spreading the wellsprings of Kabbalah outward.[4, 5, 6] The harmony between the sanctity of the "David HaMelech" beit midrash and the live digital broadcast creates a leading model for teaching Torah in our generation.[1, 4]
Institutionalising Continuity and the Doctrine of Study
The appearance of young rabbis from the Yitzchaki family giving the weekly lessons on the Zohar attests that this is not a passing phenomenon but the planned building of a scholarly and spiritual dynasty in Moshav Porat.[5] This institutionalisation ensures that the kabbalistic centre Rabbi Yitzchaki founded will continue to be a Torah beacon in the Lev HaSharon area for many years to come, while constantly developing ways of making the esoteric teaching accessible to the masses.[4, 5, 6]
